title: Morgan Stanley is not Goldman Sachs
description: Morgan Stanley posted a smaller-than-expected loss on strong revenues, sending its stock soaring.  Rival Goldman Sachs wasn't so lucky earlier this week.

asr.full_text: A smaller than expected loss for Morgan Stanley has its shares jumping off recent two-year lows. It's been a rough year for the investment bank. Shares are down about 20% year-to-date,. But investors were seizing on what they see as a buying opportunity Thursday morning. Morgan Stanley posted a loss of about a half billion dollars for the second quarter,. Mostly because of a $1.7 billion one-time charge. But it's the top-line revenue number that investors are most impressed with. Revenue rose more than 16% to just under $10 billion. That's the highest quarterly revenue since before the financial crisis hit. The bank's trading revenue rose 14%. Compare that to rival Goldman Sachs, which said trading revenue fell more than 40% last quarter. And has fallen for six straight quarters. Goldman has also had a rough year. Its shares hit a 52-week low when its earnings came out Tuesday. Morgan Stanley hopes today's solid earnings report puts its recent lows in the rearview mirror. For CNN Money, I'm Alison Kosick at the New York Stock Exchange.
